discovery: Quantum simulation of Hubbard models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and co-workers proposed in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model, with interactions and tunnelling set by laser light, and predicted a superfluid-Mott insulator transition. Bloch and Greiner observed this quantum phase transition in 2002, turning a textbook model of strongly correlated matter into a clean, tunable experiment. This work created analog quantum simulation as a field. Greiner's quantum gas microscope and Bloch's single-site-resolved imaging later gave atom-by-atom access to Mott insulators, antiferromagnetic correlations and doped Fermi-Hubbard physics, reaching regimes relevant to high-temperature superconductivity that classical computation cannot handle. Zoller's theoretical framework, including lattice gauge theories and Rydberg-based protocols, has guided the field since. Together they joined atomic physics and condensed-matter physics and made controlled many-body quantum systems a new laboratory for fundamental physics. Neutral-atom quantum computing now builds directly on these methods.
